_note: Our own invention, every word of it, and that is the whole point. This is
what check.py plays, so it has to live in the tree -- and a published
module never can. Nothing here is transcribed from anything.
It names no creature. A module from a 4e book names creatures and
cast_list resolves them against localization/names.json, but that file is
git-ignored and a fresh clone has none -- so a fixture leaning on it would
pass on this machine and fail on a clone. Specifying foes by words, role
and rank exercises the thematic and reflavour paths instead, which are the
ones that have to work for every other edition anyway.
Five scenes, covering all four kinds, with a real branch: the skill
challenge leads somewhere different depending on whether it is won.
The challenge lists four primary skills, and that is load-bearing rather
than decorative. With two (athletics and endurance) only one of the four
characters was any good at either, and the win rate by complexity ran
82/17/7/5/2 percent -- a cliff. With four that span the party it is
100/55/37/15/7, which is a difficulty ladder. The subsystem was identical
in both runs. How well the primary list spans the party is the thing that
decides whether a challenge is playable, so list the skills a published
challenge lists and do not trim them.
If you edit the prose here, check it against the localisation by hand.
The first draft invented 'river rats' and that is a printed name --
leaks.py reported the file clean, because its wide walk waives a name made
of two ordinary words. Inventing a name is not the same as inventing an
unused one. The check is one query against localisation(), and #494 is why
it cannot be the gate's job.
The yard carries affordances and an npc so check.py exercises the beat
loop rather than only the scenes that were here first. Scripted, it takes
none of them and runs to max_beats -- which is the point: the bookkeeping
is driven without pretending to a judgement no model made.

scenes.name: The Mill Yard
scenes.brief: Flood water stands knee-deep across the yard and the mill wheel has stopped turning. The miller's dog is on the roof of the cart shed and will not come down. Something has been in the cellar since the river rose, and the miller would rather pay than go down there herself.

npcs.name: the miller
npcs.wants: somebody else to go down into her cellar
npcs.voice: tired, practical, haggling out of habit
knows: the water came up three nights ago and has not gone down
something has been moving down there since
she will pay in coin and in grain
hides: she heard it before the flood and said nothing

affordances.what: push the miller for more than she first offered
affordances.win: she adds a sack of grain and the loan of a lantern to the fee
affordances.lose: the offer stands as it was and she looks away

affordances.what: study the miller for what she is not saying
affordances.win: she is frightened of the cellar in a way a flood does not explain
affordances.lose: nothing, and she notices the staring

affordances.what: get the dog down off the cart shed roof
affordances.win: the dog comes down and will not go near the cellar stair
affordances.lose: the dog stays where it is

affordances.what: stop talking and go to the wheel
affordances.win: the party crosses the yard to the mill wheel

scenes.name: Freeing the Wheel
scenes.brief: The wheel is jammed with silt and broken timber. Clearing it drains the cellar; leaving it means going down into standing water, in the dark, with whatever is already in there listening to you work.

scenes.name: The Drained Cellar
scenes.brief: The water goes out in a rush and leaves the floor slick and littered. Whatever was swimming down here is now walking, and it is not pleased about the change.
scenes.tactics: The skirmishers circle and bite at whoever is furthest from the stair. The soldier holds the stair itself and does not leave it.

scenes.name: The Flooded Cellar
scenes.brief: The wheel is still jammed and the cellar is still full. You go down into it anyway, by lantern light, and everything down here heard you coming.
scenes.tactics: They have had time to spread out. The soldiers take the stair from both sides and the skirmishers come from behind the grain bins.

scenes.name: Five Minutes on the Stair
scenes.brief: Long enough to bind a wound and get your breath back. Not long enough to get a daily power back, and not long enough for the thing in the loft to lose interest.

scenes.name: The Grain Loft
scenes.brief: The ladder comes up through the floor into the dark under the roof beams, and it is the only way up or down.
scenes.tactics: The elite stays beyond the lantern and spends its minions to keep the ladder head crowded.
